entry_points.name: close_account
entry_points.note: Takes a session and a user id and writes to the user row; app.py registers the module it lives in.

stores.name: users

fields.name: deleted_at
fields.note: Soft-delete marker the application writes on the row; the erasure verdict turns on this column.

erasure.note: close_account sets deleted_at to the current time and is_active to False and commits; the row and its email, name and phone columns stay, and no scheduled job in this repository deletes them later.

stores.note: SQLAlchemy table holding one row per account holder.

stores.name: tickets

fields.name: subject
fields.note: Ticket title typed by the person; the schema does not constrain what it holds.

fields.name: body
fields.note: Ticket text typed by the person; the schema does not constrain what it holds.

fields.name: opened_at
fields.note: Records when the person opened the ticket.

erasure.note: The only deletion entry point writes a soft-delete marker on the user row and never deletes it, and the User.tickets relationship carries no cascade argument, so the ticket rows stay.

stores.note: SQLAlchemy table holding support tickets, each carrying a user_id foreign key to users.id.
